"WORLD WAR II: 1944–1945 — REALISTIC LARGE-SCALE BATTLEFIELD GAME

1. Main Menu

The game is set during World War II, specifically between 1944 and 1945.

The game starts with the screen displayed upside down. The player must rotate their phone 180 degrees to begin playing.

The main menu has three buttons:

- PLAY
- SETTINGS
- HELP

All menus and interface elements are initially in English. In Settings, the player can change the language to Russian.

2. Team Selection

When the player presses PLAY, they can choose between two factions:

- USSR (Soviet Union)
- GERMANY

Each faction has historically inspired weapons, uniforms, military vehicles, aircraft, and equipment from 1944–1945.

3. Maps and Environment

The game features a huge, detailed battlefield with realistic World War II environments.

The map includes:

- Large trench systems.
- Destroyable 20th-century houses and buildings.
- Fields, forests, roads, and open terrain.
- Military bases and strategic control points.
- Machine-gun positions.
- Defensive structures and artillery positions.

Players and AI soldiers can dig trenches during battles.

Buildings can be damaged and destroyed by tanks, artillery, and aircraft.

The environment should look realistic and highly detailed.

4. Gameplay and Main Objectives

The game is played entirely from a first-person perspective.

Each team has 50 AI soldiers, not including the human player.

Both teams have identical main objectives:

- Capture strategic control points.
- Defend their own positions.
- Attack enemy positions.
- Capture the enemy's main base.

The battle continues indefinitely until one team captures the enemy's main base.

AI soldiers must behave realistically, cooperate with their teammates, use weapons, operate vehicles, and fight for objectives.

5. Military Vehicles

Both factions have their own historically inspired military vehicles.

USSR Vehicles

GAZ-67 Military Vehicle

- An open military vehicle.
- Can transport up to four soldiers, including the driver.
- AI soldiers can enter and operate the vehicle.
- The human player can drive it using the same controls as AI soldiers.

T-34-85 Tank

- A highly detailed 3D model.
- Realistic tank physics and damage simulation.
- AI soldiers can operate the tank.
- A maximum of four AI soldiers can occupy the tank.
- If a human player enters the tank, the player controls it alone.

German Vehicles

German Motorcycle with Sidecar

- Can transport two soldiers.
- The sidecar can have a mounted machine gun.
- A soldier sitting in the sidecar can operate the machine gun.

Panther Ausf. D Tank

- Highly detailed 3D model.
- Realistic armor and internal damage simulation.
- AI soldiers can operate all tank positions.

6. Aircraft and Pilots

Both teams can use aircraft.

Each team can have up to five aircraft pilots.

Soviet Aircraft

Ilyushin Il-2

A ground-attack aircraft equipped with unguided rockets.

Its rockets are effective against both infantry and military vehicles.

After firing its rockets, the pilot can:

- Make another attack run and use the aircraft's machine guns against infantry and lightly armored vehicles.
- Return to the airfield to rearm and prepare for another mission.

The aircraft must have realistic flight physics and damage.

Aircraft damage must include detachable and destructible components:

- Wings.
- Tail.
- Engine.
- Other aircraft components.

When severely damaged, aircraft should behave realistically. They can spin out of control, catch fire, crash, or break apart during impact.

Pilots can eject from the aircraft or exit it after landing, provided the aircraft is still in a condition that allows them to survive.

Aircraft must also be able to crash into buildings, damaging the structure and potentially starting fires.

German Aircraft

Messerschmitt Bf 109

A German fighter aircraft used to attack enemy aircraft and infantry.

Mistel Aircraft

A special aircraft configuration involving a piloted aircraft and an explosive unmanned in

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable WWII battlefield game set in 1944–1945, or adapt the existing game to match the request.

## Requirements
- Start on an upside-down screen requiring a 180° phone rotation; main menu has PLAY, SETTINGS, HELP, initially in English, with Russian available in Settings.
- PLAY leads to USSR or GERMANY faction selection; factions have historically inspired 1944–1945 equipment.
- Provide a large, detailed battlefield with trenches, destructible buildings, terrain, bases, control points, machine-gun positions, and artillery; players and AI can dig trenches.
- Entirely first-person gameplay; 50 AI soldiers per team (excluding the player), with coordinated combat and objectives to capture control points, defend, attack, and capture the enemy base; battle continues until the enemy base is captured.
- Include USSR GAZ-67 (four occupants) and T-34-85 (up to four AI crew); German motorcycle with sidecar (two occupants and optional sidecar machine gun) and Panther Ausf. D; AI and player vehicle operation as specified.
- Include up to five pilots per team, Soviet Il-2 and German Bf 109 and Mistel aircraft; aircraft should support realistic flight, damage, component destruction, crashes, rearming, and pilot exit/ejection as described. The Mistel description is truncated at “explosive unmanned in”.

- Turn the existing WWII battlefield prototype into a 3D game and add mobile joystick and fire-button controls.

## Requirements
- Set in 1944–1945, with an upside-down start screen, English/Russian interface, and USSR/Germany selection.
- First-person battlefield gameplay with AI squads, combat, trenches, vehicles, aircraft, and capture objectives.
- Add a mobile joystick for movement and a button for shooting.

- Use Three.js for a lightweight, low-poly 3D browser implementation.
- Keep the existing menu and HUD styling; reuse its touch-control elements for mobile input.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added Three.js-based 3D battlefield implementation in `three-game.js`.
- Updated `index.html` to load the 3D implementation.
- Added touch joystick movement and fire-button handlers in the 3D implementation.

### Active
- Verify the 3D game runs in-browser and that joystick and fire controls work; check for runtime errors.

- (none)

1. Run syntax checks and open the game in a browser.

- `index.html`: Game page, menus, HUD, and touch-control elements.
- `three-game.js`: Three.js scene, battlefield simulation, controls, and combat.
- `game.js`: Earlier 2D implementation, superseded by `three-game.js`.

The 3D game loads in a headless browser, and `three-game.js` passes the JavaScript syntax check. I also updated the touch controls to prevent browser gestures from interfering, and the joystick now shows its movement direction.

I couldn’t verify the menu flow or touch interactions end-to-end in a real device. Mobile movement and firing are implemented; aiming still uses the mouse, and vehicles remain visual rather than drivable.
